name: RoboForce TITAN
summary: A two-armed industrial robot with a liftable waist on a wheeled or tracked all-terrain base, built for outdoor work such as utility-scale solar construction, with a 40 kg peak dual-arm payload and 8 h per battery pack.

germany.statusNote: No German or EU seller, distributor or price found. RoboForce (Milpitas, California) takes enquiries through its contact form; its March 2026 funding news speaks of moving active pilot programmes toward production deployments, with no European sales route named.

specs.label: Manipulation precision
specs.quote: It can achieve 1 mm (0.03 in.) precision for fine-grained manipulation

specs.label: Base options
specs.quote: The mobile manipulator comes in wheeled and tracked base variations, with more on the way.

specs.label: Primitive skills
specs.quote: Titan delivers five key primitive capabilities—pick, place, press, twist, and connect—essential for most industrial tasks

notes: Wheels and tracks are alternative base options, not both on one unit.
The 40 kg figure is a peak value for both arms together; no per-arm payload is published, so armPayloadKg stays empty.
RoboForce describes 'expert robotic hands built for industrial applications'; the hand type (gripper or multi-finger) is not specified.
The Robot Report calls TITAN a mobile manipulator; it is listed here as a wheeled humanoid because it has a waist with two arms and a lifting torso.

evidence.task: Construction, inspection and maintenance work on utility-scale solar farms
evidence.note: Target market on the maker's solutions page; no named solar customer or published pilot result found.

evidence.task: Material handling, installation support and site inspection on construction sites

researchEvidence.quote: an AI robot for industrial deployments in demanding outdoor environments
